Visiting the sick Sa'd, whose only heir was a daughter, the Prophet limited his bequest in charity to one third, heirs being better left rich, and pitied Sa'd bin Khaula.
Wills are to be written within two nights; the Prophet left little and bequeathed Allah's Book; Aisha denies a will for Ali; Sa'd's bequest is limited to a third.
Visiting Sa'd, gravely ill in the Farewell Hajj, the Prophet limits his charity of his wealth to a third, as leaving heirs rich is better than leaving them poor.
Asked if the Prophet made a will, Abdullah bin Abi Aufa first says no, then that he made a will recommending Allah's Book.
Gravely ill, Sa'd was told even a third in charity is too much, since leaving heirs rich is better, and the Prophet prayed his companions' emigration be completed.
Near death with one daughter as heir, Sa'd was allowed to give a third in charity, though even that is much, as heirs are better left rich than poor.
